# Development workflow

[Wiki home](README.md) | [Edit source](../../AGENTS.md)

## Conventions / gotchas (learned the hard way)

- One MonoBehaviour/NetworkBehaviour per file, file name = class name (otherwise "missing script" on prefabs).
- Server RPCs: `[Rpc(SendTo.Server, InvokePermission = RpcInvokePermission.Everyone)]` + `RpcParams rp` → `rp.Receive.SenderClientId`.
- Never write NetworkVariables before spawn: store them in pending fields, then apply them in `OnNetworkSpawn`.
- Don't use `??` / `?.` on UnityEngine.Object.
- TMP: ASCII glyphs only (no `…`, arrows, emoji) → otherwise missing-glyph warnings.
- PrefabBuilder deletes prefabs before re-saving them (keeps `GlobalObjectIdHash` valid). Network prefab list is rebuilt from scratch.
- Skybox shader must handle reversed-Z (otherwise it draws over everything).
- **Art direction (#120, rules in "Art & assets" below and `Assets/Design/DESIGN.md` "Visual Identity"): low poly, flat-shaded with the shared palette (variant A, 2026-10-17).** It replaces the detailed PBR direction of #91. Everything the bullets below describe as Fab/Sketchfab/Poly Haven assets, PBR materials, photo textures or scans (#91-#100) is the legacy look and gets replaced by #122-#127/#133; keep their runtime code, swap models/materials.
- Low-poly ships (#122, 2026-10-17, placeholder look - the ships get another pass): `Art/Palette.json` = the shared palette (read by `vw_blender.load_palette` and `ContentBuilder.Pal`). `Tools/Blender/lowpoly_ships.py` turns Quaternius "Ultimate Spaceships" (CC0, `Tools/Blender/Sources/Quaternius/`) into `Art/Models/Ships/LowPoly/Ship_<Dart|Mule|Nostos>_LP(.fbx|_Canopy.fbx)`: scaled to length, every face recoloured from its texture to a palette class, canopy faces split off (`canopy` = dark faces in a source-space box, `glass_box` = faces facing up/forward or `glass_dark` in a Unity-space box), prints sizes in Unity coordinates. `Tools/Blender/lowpoly_kit.py` converts the Kenney Space Station Kit (zip in `Sources/KenneyStationKit/`) to `Art/Models/Kit/Kit_<name>.fbx` (Kenney units, a wall tile = 1). `LowPolyShipBuilder` (partial `ContentBuilder`): `VW_LowPoly` material, `LowPolyMesh`, `KitMesh`/`KitPart`, `BuildLowPolyDart` (Omen, 15 m, eye `DartLPEye`) and `BuildLowPolyMule` (Spitfire, 13 m, `MuleLPEye`) with `LowPolyCockpit` (tub, Kenney chair + console, live screens, own stick/throttle with grip IK); `BuildDart`/`BuildMule` prefer them, the Fab/R35 builds stay as fallback. The Nostos still uses the Ark: its interior, airlock and clamps are fitted to the Ark hull, so the Imperial hull is prepared but not wired.
- Legacy PBR asset pipeline (#91, being replaced, see "Art & assets"): source files in the repo (models: `Tools/Blender/Sources/<Asset>/`, textures: `Assets/_Project/Art/Models/<Group>/<Asset>/`), a `Tools/Blender/<asset>.py` script normalizes the model (metres, nose Blender -Y = Unity +Z, origin at the bounds centre, target size) and exports `Assets/_Project/Art/Models/<Group>/<Name>.fbx`. `AssetModelBuilder` (partial `ContentBuilder`): `ModelMesh(fbx)` (own UVs/normals, MikkTSpace tangents), `ImportTexture(path, srgb, normal, flipGreen)`, `PackMetallicSmoothness` (Substance metallic + roughness -> URP map, generated PNG), `PbrMaterial(name, dir, prefix)` = URP Lit from a `<prefix>_Base_color/Metallic/Roughness/Normal_DirectX/Mixed_AO/Emissive.jpg` set (DirectX normals are green-flipped by the importer). `PrefabBuilder` places colliders/seats/muzzles/thrusters/lights around the asset and keeps the procedural build as fallback when the FBX is missing (`BuildDart` -> `BuildFabDart`). Cockpits: the pilot sits inside. `fab_spaceship.py` cuts the canopy glass out of the hull (faces in a box whose texture is dark = painted glass) into `*_Canopy.fbx` (smoked `VOIDWARD/Glass`), and builds `*_Cockpit.fbx` = the hull section between two bulkheads, duplicated, flipped and pushed inwards, capped (vw vertex contract, `VW_HullInterior` = VW_Hull without rim); seat, consoles, stick come from `FabDartCockpitMesh`, plus the usual `Dashboard`. The script prints cross-sections (roof/floor/width per z) for placing seat and eye (anchor = eye - 1.2). Check with `ContentBuilder.PreviewShot("<prefab>", camLocal, targetLocal, fov, name)` -> `Temp/HeroShots`.
- Mule + Ark (#97, the Ark is the Nostos since #49): the Mule is the Fab DROPSHIP R35 (`Tools/Blender/r35_dropship.py`: 15 m, the upper nose cut out as the canopy, cockpit tub = shrunk convex hull of the nose section, open under the canopy, because the R35 hull has deep insets), `BuildR35Mule` puts the Dart's fittings on a raised deck via `DartFittings(root, dartHull, walls)` (the Dart fittings in Dart coordinates under a root moved so the Dart eye (0, 0, 3.67) lands on the ship's eye). The Ark is the Sketchfab SPACESHIP - CARGO (`Tools/Blender/cargo_ark.py`: posed rig baked, native 36 m, hull faces inside the walkable volume removed, window cut out, airlock door cut into the left flank between the wings); `BuildCargoArk` builds the deck shell (`ArkDeckMesh`: corridor with a chamfered ceiling, bridge with raised pilot platform, airlock + boarding ramp, stations), a hollow collider shell, three gravity volumes (corridor, bridge, airlock), turret/engineer seats with the Dart chair (`ArkChairAt`). The Ark constants (`ArkFloor`, `ArkHall*`, `ArkBridge*`, `ArkDoor*`) must match `cargo_ark.py` ROOMS/DOOR. Derelict Ark = the same prefab: `ShipDerelictLook` (Ship) swaps hull + deck to `ArkDerelictMaterial` / `InteriorDerelictMaterial` and the cabin lights to flickering red emergency light while `ShipCore.Derelict` is set. Interiors seen from inside must be closed by own walls: the hull's back faces are culled (you would see space).
- Enemies + Warden (#98): assets from Sketchfab glTF (CC BY), normalized by `Tools/Blender/enemy_assets.py` (`--ingest <Downloads>` once: sources zipped to `Tools/Blender/Sources/Enemies/<Name>.zip` without textures, textures as 2K JPG to `Art/Models/Enemies/<Name>/<material>_<baseColor|normal|metallicRoughness|emissive>.jpg`; then a plain run rebuilds every FBX). Swarm hunter (PirateFighter, I_Ship), swarm brood ship (PirateGunship, E_Ship_A), squid (FlyingCritter) = static PBR; crawler (Insectoid), spitter (Alien Ninja), nest guardian (Frost Predator, Rigify -> `rebake_rest` onto the idle pose) = rigged walkers; Warden boss = "alien droneship" (5 chunks decimated to 60k, every face doubled flipped because the source shells are single-sided, vw vertex contract ivory/cyan, crevice glow from the AO bake). Sentinel (DroneSwarm) = own build `Tools/Blender/warden_sentinel.py` (+ `Enemy_Sentinel_Ring.fbx`). Unity side `EnemyModelBuilder` (partial `ContentBuilder`): `EnemyMaterials` (URP Lit per glTF material, cull off), `PrepareEnemyRig` (Generic, used clips, motion node = the run cycle's travelling node so clips play in place), `EnemyController` (Speed blend idle/walk/run, Cycle offset, Attack/Alert triggers), `EnemyModel` ("Model" child, null -> legacy mesh). Runtime `EnemyAnimator` (AI, every peer): Speed from the interpolated motion, `EnemyBrain.AttackAnimClientRpc` -> Attack trigger or procedural lunge, Alert (roar) on Patrol -> Chase, floaters swim, ships bank. `SpinPart` (Core) spins the sentinel halo and the boss rings. Blender pitfalls: the Sketchfab scenes carry a scene-sized "Icosphere" helper (only skinned meshes count), the importer stacks every clip as NLA tracks, and animation lives on the evaluated copy (`evaluated_get`) - original pose bones / `modifier_apply` see the rest pose.
- World objects + POIs (#99): Sketchfab assets (CC BY) normalized by `Tools/Blender/world_assets.py` (`--ingest <Downloads>` takes glTF zips and original FBX downloads: sources to `Tools/Blender/Sources/World/<Name>.zip`, textures as 2K JPG to `Art/Models/World/<Name>/<material>_<baseColor|normal|metallicRoughness|emissive|ao>.jpg`; FBX texture sets are mapped per asset in `ASSETS` (UE DirectX normals flipped, specular/gloss packed to metallicRoughness, `"auto"` = the FBX's own links + flat 4x4 maps); a plain run rebuilds every FBX and prints the numbers PrefabBuilder uses). `World_Station` (Space Station 3, twin rings, 64 m, spins via `TraderStation.spinner`, static MeshCollider copy), `World_Pad` (teleporter pad = landing deck, origin = deck centre; station deck at y -6.5, z 52, Wasp cockpit console as trader terminal), `World_Wreck` (+ `_Chunks`, `World_Scrap` = torn Vigilant destroyer section), `World_Ruin` (Ancient Relic, untextured -> vw vertex contract ivory/cyan like the Warden, `ImportedMesh` + `MatHull`), `World_Nest` (alien eggs), `World_Crate` (+ `_Lid`, hinge (0, 1.118, -0.725)), `World_Rock` (photoscan, node base), `World_Battery` (fuel node canister, generic pickup cell, `fuel` item), `World_Medkit` (medkit tool = `ToolModel(3)`, `medkit` item). Crashed ship = the Fab Dart wrecked and posed by `Tools/Blender/crashed_dart.py` (`Ship_Dart_Crashed*.fbx`, scorch = generated texture `CrashedDartMaterial`, smoke `SmokeColumn`). Unity: `WorldModelBuilder` (`WorldModel`/`WorldModelSolid`/`WorldMesh`, materials via the shared `GltfMaterials`, cut-out parts share a texture folder via `WorldTextureSet`), `WorldPrefabBuilder` (`BuildAsset*`, PrefabBuilder picks them when the FBX exists, else the procedural build). Item models from assets set `ItemDef.ModelMaterials` (WorldPickup swaps mesh + materials; items without a model show the `generic` cell). POI spawn offsets in `SystemDirector` (ruin cache, crash crate/scrap, wreck crates/nodes/pickups) follow the asset sizes. Gotcha: `CrewController()` recreates its asset - reuse `crewCtrl` (or load the controller) outside BuildPawn, else the pawn prefab loses its controller.
- Procedural fallback (legacy hero pipeline #26, still used by the astronaut, Mule, Ark, props): build with `Hero()` (weighted normals via `SmoothAngle`, panel detail) and the parametric parts `AddLoft` (fuselages, limbs), `AddLathe` (nozzles, rings, tanks), `AddSlab` (wings, plates), `AddTube`/`Polyline`, liveries via quad-aware `Paint`. Render with `MatHull` (VW_ToonFlat `_SURFACEDETAIL_ON`: triplanar panel seams/rivets/grime from `SurfaceDetailBuilder`, edge wear on chamfers, GGX + probe reflections). Primitives choose winding from geometry, so mirrored matrices (`Scale(-1,1,1)`) are fine. Iterate with menu `Voidward/Dev/Hero Preview Shots` (renders to `Temp/HeroShots`, no full rebuild needed); after Build All Content, `ContentBuilder.PreviewPrefabs("<name filter>")` / `PreviewShot(...)` (callable from RunCommand) render built prefabs. Ship exhaust and projectiles = `VW_Plume` (additive fresnel). Soot/burns: `MeshBuilder.Weather`; contact shading: `Grade`. Planet decor, landmarks, asteroids and the menu ground use `VW_Terrain` with a rock detail mask (enable via `MeshBuilder.Panel = 1`). Per-sector color grading lives in `PaletteDef` (runtime volume in `SectorVisuals`).
- Editor ↔ release build = "NetworkConfig mismatch". Use a Development build (`Voidward/Build/macOS (Development)` or `Windows (x64, Development)`) or MPPM.
- Owning a ship in its spawn frame breaks positioning for remote clients → `RunManager.SeatLater` delays it by 0.6 s.

## Issue workflow (mandatory)

Repo: `Weofi/Space-Beyond-Infinity`, default branch `main`. When the user hands over an issue:
1. Read the issue (incl. images/mockups) via `gh issue view <nr> --comments`.
2. `git checkout main && git pull`, then create a dedicated branch `issue-<nr>-<short-slug>` (never work on `main`).
3. Push the branch early and open a **draft PR** against `main` with `Closes #<nr>` in the body (check for a PR template first).
4. Implement on that branch with small, descriptive commits (`#<nr>: ...`), push regularly.
5. When done: compile check + test per the "Testing playbook" (cheapest level first, not a full run), update the PR description (changes, test notes, screenshots), mark it ready for review.
6. If everything works and the issue is fully done: merge the PR into `main` yourself (user-approved), then `git checkout main && git pull`. If anything is broken or open, don't merge; report back instead.
One issue = one branch = one PR. Don't mix issues.

## Agent workflow (Unity MCP)

- Don't edit C# while Unity is in Play Mode (a domain reload breaks statics).
- Compile check: read `Logs/Editor.log` after the last "Requested script compilation" and grep `): error CS`.
- `Unity_RunCommand` returns "Unity not detected" while compiling/reloading → just retry. System.Reflection is not allowed there.
- Run menu items (`Voidward/Build All Content`, `Voidward/Build/...`) via ManageMenuItem, not RunCommand. Exception: dev builds, see the testing playbook.
- Never call `AssetDatabase.Refresh`/`ImportAsset` in Play Mode: it can trigger a script recompile + domain reload that breaks the session (UIRoot NREs). Shader tweaks: exit Play Mode first, or check them in Edit Mode (render a quad with the material).
- Target: zero console errors/warnings from Voidward code. Known foreign noise: AI Inference tensor warnings, PreviewRenderUtility leak.
- Unity skills (`.agents/skills`, from `Unity-Technologies/skills`, lock: `skills-lock.json`): use them as domain knowledge only. Implement their recommendations in the builder code (`ContentBuilder`/`PrefabBuilder`/`SceneBuilder`) or in runtime code, never as direct edits to generated scenes/prefabs/assets. Update: `npx skills update -p`.

## Cross-platform (Mac + Windows)

- Same Unity version on both machines (`ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`). Line endings are pinned to LF via `.gitattributes`.
- Before switching machines: commit + push. On the other machine: `git pull` first, then open Unity.
- `.mcp.json` is git-ignored (machine-specific Unity relay path); each machine keeps its own.
- GitHub: use the GitHub CLI (`gh`, logged in via `gh auth login --web`) for issues, PRs and merges. No GitHub MCP server (its OAuth needs dynamic client registration, which Claude Code can't do with GitHub). On Windows, `gh` lives at `C:\Program Files\GitHub CLI\gh.exe` (call it by full path if PATH isn't refreshed yet).
- Blender: Windows `C:\Program Files\Blender Foundation\Blender 5.2\blender.exe`; Mac `/Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender` (install the same 5.2 version there).
